text.p: More than 5,000 police and paramilitary troops took to the streets of Dhaka to prevent violence as an opposition-led strike virtually paralysed the country on Thursday, police and government officials said.
The main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) called the work stoppage to protest against higher taxes in the government budget.
The strike shut Bangladesh's foreign exchange market and suspended trading on the Dhaka and Chittagong stock exchanges.
The strikers halted all road transportation except for rickshaws. Many residents of the capital Dhaka were seen walking to work.
Communication Ministry officials said most trains and other modes of transport had moved out of their terminals in the early morning.
But they said hundreds of people were stranded as inter-district bus services were suspended by the strike. "The road communications have been badly affected," one official said.
The police said more than 100 people were injured in pre-strike violence on Wednesday.
They said the people were hurt when BNP activists clashed with supporters of the ruling Awami League in Narayanganj near Dhaka and in southern Barisal town.
"There has been no violence so far today. It looks peaceful except for a few incidents of deflating rickshaw tyres by strikers," a police officer said.
The BNP of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia called Thursday's work stoppage to protest what it calls an "anti-people" budget passed by parliament on Monday.

The BNP had sought the withdrawal of a 2.5 percent infrastructure development tax on imports and some locally produced goods and services, which Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria proposed when unveiling the budget last month.
BNP Secretary General Abdul Mannan said on Tuesday -- the first day of Bangladesh's fiscal 1997/98 year -- that the budget was against the interests of the country.
"The budget will deter investment and it will make the country dependent on others," he told party supporters.
